name: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
problem: Sequence-level KD suffers a train/inference mismatch: the student is trained on a FIXED set of output sequences but generates its own at inference, and the errors compound.
mechanism: Generalized Knowledge Distillation (GKD): instead of training only on the fixed output set, train the student on its OWN generated sequences with teacher feedback on those sequences - so the teacher supervises exactly the states the student actually reaches. Because the loss is decoupled from the on-policy data, ANY student-teacher divergence can be substituted, which matters when the student lacks the expressivity to match the teacher's distribution. The same objective composes with RL fine-tuning, letting distillation and RLHF run as one loop.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): GKD addresses the distribution mismatch by training on self-generated sequences with teacher feedback, offers flexibility to employ alternative loss functions 'when the student lacks the expressivity to mimic the teacher's distribution', and integrates seamlessly with RLHF; demonstrated on summarization, translation, arithmetic reasoning, and task-agnostic instruction-tuning distillation. No numeric accuracy delta in the abstract.
